title: [3/8/2024] The production levels of the main kinds of fuel
prompt: The graph below shows the production levels of the main kinds of fuel in the UK between 1981 and 2000. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the production levels of three different types of fuel in the UK over a 19-year period from 1981 to 2000, measured in energy units.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while petroleum remained the dominant fuel source throughout the period, coal production showed a marked decline, and natural gas witnessed a steady increase.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the major fuel source, petroleum started at approximately 90 energy units in 1981. The output of petroleum then followed a fluctuating pattern, rising to peaks of about 140 units in 1986 and 1996, with a trough of roughly 100 units in 1991, before stabilizing at around 140 units by 2000.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining sources, natural gas production began at the lowest level among the three fuels, at about 40 energy units in 1981, while coal began at around 80 units. However, natural gas demonstrated a consistent upward trend, particularly after 1991, when it surpassed coal production. By 2000, natural gas production had reached roughly 100 energy units, making it the second most produced fuel in the UK. Meanwhile, coal production experienced a continuous decline over the period, dropping sharply to 40 units by 1983, showing a brief recovery to 60 units in 1986, before declining further to end the period at approximately 35 units.
